terms.meaning: Values a component remembers while it is on screen.
The element that keyboard and screen reader users are currently on.

used_by: src/app/register/page.tsx sends new users here through the onboarding route.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Onboarding imports
sections.what: Brings in the navigation tool, the state and focus helpers, the pictogram components, and the sport type. The file is marked to run in the browser.
sections.why: Likely reason: the screens respond to clicks and move focus, so they run in the browser.

sections.name: SPORTS
sections.title: Sports offered
sections.what: Lists the five sports a user can follow: cricket, football, basketball, Formula 1, and tennis, each with a display name.
sections.why: Likely reason: a fixed list of supported sports, shown as checkboxes on the last screen.
sections.watch_out: Each sport key is passed to the pictogram component, so a new sport needs a matching picture or it will show without one.

sections.name: STEPS
sections.title: Three intro screens
sections.what: Holds the three intro screens: making the call before it happens, grading the decision and not the luck, and choosing sports and language. Each has a title, a short body, and small pictures.
sections.why: Likely reason: it explains the core idea of the product before users set their preferences.
sections.watch_out: The number of progress dots comes from this list, so adding or removing a screen changes them automatically.

sections.name: Onboarding
sections.title: Stepping through and saving choices
sections.what: Shows one screen at a time with Back and Next. On the last screen it shows the sport checkboxes, the language choice, and a Start button that is off until at least one sport is ticked. Start saves the choices and moves on. Focus moves to each new heading, and an error appears if saving fails.
sections.why: Focus moves so keyboard and screen reader users land on the new screen. The code comment says it is done on step changes and not on first load. Likely reason for the disabled Start: the app needs at least one sport.
sections.watch_out: Cricket starts ticked, so a user who never looks at the sports list may save cricket only.

summary: A three-screen welcome that ends with choosing sports and language and saving them.
purpose: Introduces the product and records the user's sports and language before they start.
why: New users need to understand the idea and set their preferences once.
how: Steps in order: the screen shows step one of three with the progress dots. Next and Back move between screens, and focus moves to each new heading. On the last screen, the user ticks sports and chooses a language. Start saves the choices to the preferences endpoint, then goes to the requested page. If saving fails, an error message appears.
inputs: The next address passed in from the onboarding route, the user's clicks, the sports they tick, and their language choice.
outputs: Saved preferences on the server, a move to the next page, or an error message.
risks: Cricket is pre-selected, so a user who does not look may save only cricket. The Hindi option is offered, but whether the rest of the app supports it is not visible here.
debug: If Start stays disabled, check the sports list. If saving fails, check the response from the preferences endpoint. If focus jumps oddly, check the heading focus effect.
